cues.text: Watch F1 Finance's tax machine prepare a Seattle city tax return.
Next, the quarter's books: every billing agrees with the ledger and the state returns already filed. Seattle charges its own B&O tax, business and occupation tax, on gross receipts.
Now it checks the city's rules. Four are confirmed online and six from a saved copy; three questions are left for a person.
Apportionment means taxing only the work done in Seattle, so jobs in other cities are deducted. One invoice coded to Bellevue was really a Seattle job. The city tax is $44,166.
Ten checks pass, with one invoice moved to Seattle.
Last, it writes the draft return and its workpapers.

All done. The draft shows $44,166 of Seattle tax for the quarter. Six items stay open, including a job that straddles the city line, a bad debt to confirm, and a late fee of about $3,975 the city will add. A person reviews, signs and files; nothing is filed or paid.
